abstract: Five compared theorems. Among all substitutions on at most three letters whose incidence matrix has a Pisot eigenvalue θ > 1, the least such θ is the plastic number ρ, the real root of x³ = x + 1, attained only by the Padovan rule a ↦ b, b ↦ c, c ↦ ab and its mirror c ↦ ba, up to renaming the letters; both minimal rules are chiral, in opposite directions. Precisely: (1) for a substitution σ on k ≤ 3 letters (images may be empty) and a real eigenvalue θ > 1 of its integer incidence matrix that is a Pisot number, ρ ≤ θ, and θ = ρ exactly when, after renaming the letters, σ is the Padovan rule or its mirror; no primitivity or unit hypothesis; (2) the same classification for every real eigenvalue, with no Pisot hypothesis; (3) a 3 × 3 natural matrix with characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1 is the Padovan matrix after one simultaneous permutation of rows and columns; (4) Siegel's bound ρ ≤ θ for Pisot numbers of degree at most three (Siegel 1944, restricted; not new; proved through the minimal Mahler measures of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-31-000004); (5) under the Padovan rule the word ca is a factor of the fifth iterate from the seed a, and ac is a factor of no iterate from any seed; under its mirror, the reverse. The uniqueness was stated without proof by Mercat (2020) for substitutions on three letters; the contribution is a kernel-checked proof of the combined statement, for every real eigenvalue and with no primitivity, unit or non-erasing hypothesis (in the equality case these are consequences: θ = ρ forces k = 3 and characteristic polynomial x³ − x − 1), together with the chirality of both minimal rules. No first-formalization claim is made. That ρ itself is a Pisot eigenvalue of the Padovan matrix, so that the bound is attained, is proved in Supplement.lean and not compared. Companion of registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006.

related_formalizations.identifier: Registered entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (stalex444/arithmetic-of-time, registered revision c48eb12817dd1d7ff3dc4d92306c7a4f249e6d7d)
related_formalizations.note: COMPANION ENTRY. Its compared statements are the successor invariant, the chirality pair and the absence of long palindromic factors for the Padovan substitution. The Padovan half of compared statement 5 here is its compared chirality statement, restated over sub s; the mirror half and statements 1-4 are not compared there. The proof modules Chirality, Irreducibility and Settling are that revision's files with the module-system header (module / public import / @[expose] public section) the registry now requires, and one proof repair in Irreducibility (quartic_irred_zmod2, linear case: simp no longer closes the goal at this toolchain; the simp call drops neg_add_cancel and zero_mul and is followed by `exact mul_eq_zero_of_left (neg_add_cancel a) _`), statement unchanged. The README's Scope section is that entry's, verbatim; its one relative link, to the paper directory, now points into the companion repository at the registered revision.

The minimal Mahler measures in degrees 2 and 3 (PDT.Mahler.quadratic_mahler_min', PDT.Mahler.cubic_mahler_min') are the engine of compared statement 4 and hence of the bound in statement 1. The seven modules PdtMahler, PdtMahlerBox, PdtMahlerMain, PdtMahlerTheta, PdtMahlerWindow, PdtPisotBoundary and PdtIrreducible are that revision's files with every statement and proof unchanged apart from the module-system header and, in PdtIrreducible, the same proof repair in quartic_irred_zmod2; PdtMahler, PdtMahlerMain, PdtMahlerTheta and PdtMahlerWindow also carry docstring edits that remove internal cross-references of the author's working notes. None of that entry's statements is re-compared here.

related_formalizations.identifier: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4 (Matrix.charpoly, Polynomial.aeval, minpoly, Polynomial.aroots, Polynomial.natDegree, IsIntegral, Polynomial.mahlerMeasure, Nat.iterate)
related_formalizations.note: The compared statements use Mathlib and core Lean vocabulary plus four short definitions in Challenge.lean (s, mir, inc, sub), each a one-line list or matrix construction stated in full there and repeated verbatim in Solution.lean. The pinned source of the imported definitions the statements rest on (Matrix.charmatrix and Matrix.charpoly, Polynomial.eval₂ and Polynomial.aeval, minpoly, Polynomial.roots and Polynomial.aroots, Polynomial.degree and Polynomial.natDegree, IsIntegral, the norm on ℂ, Nat.iterate, and core Lean's List.IsInfix, List.countP and List.count) is quoted verbatim, with permalinks, in MATHLIB_DEFINITIONS.md; the remaining vocabulary (List.map, List.reverse, List.flatten, Equiv, Matrix.map, Fin, the !![…] notation) is standard and is not quoted. DefinitionAudit.lean kernel-checks the facts the statements rely on. Mathlib contains no Pisot theory at the pin, so Siegel's theorem is not in Mathlib; the Mahler-measure route uses Mathlib's Polynomial.mahlerMeasure.

title: The Arithmetic of Time: the slowest settling clock on at most three letters is the Padovan substitution, unique up to mirror image, and both minimal rules are chiral
